most_likely_actual_diagnosis_free_text: Acute DIC with shock after povidone-iodine was pushed under pressure into the renal pelvis and absorbed into the blood (iodine toxicity or an anaphylactoid reaction). The alternative is endotoxin release or bacteremia from the pressurized instillation, causing septic shock with DIC.
one_line_reason: Rigors started within minutes of pressurized povidone-iodine instillation through the nephrostomy, followed by diffuse oozing (high INR/aPTT, low platelets), refractory shock and a rising creatinine. This points to acute DIC from systemic absorption of the iodine or of endotoxin. No listed item names DIC or iodine toxicity; bacterial sepsis is the only partial fit.
